drafts.walkScript: At line 24 Scrooge looks 'cautiously behind' the door before he shuts it. Yet at line 26 he says 'Pooh, pooh' as if it were nothing. At lines 34 and 35 he checks under the bed and in the closet. At line 53 he says 'Humbug', and at line 67 'It's humbug still'. So he calls it nonsense, but he still keeps on checking.

At line 24 the narrator 'did not dare' laugh, being a guest in the house. Line 41 gives the Captain's reply, and line 49 gives the answer from Miss Jenkyns. Neither side is ever called right. At line 50 the narrator reports the worst words but 'won't vouch for the fact'. So the whole quarrel is told, with no verdict on who was right.

Lines 12 and 13 give Rebecca's age and size, seen from outside. At lines 28 and 29 her mother sums her up to Mr Cobb. At lines 57 and 58 her feelings come only in her own spoken words. At line 60 the thought that arrives is Mr Cobb's, not hers. So her words are heard, but the passage never goes inside her head.

At line 29 Stuart would bet 'four thousand pounds'. At line 46 Fogg raises it to 'twenty thousand'. Yet at line 40 his answer is 'Deal over again', about the cards. At line 81, with the bet signed, he says 'Diamonds are trumps'. So the stakes keep rising, but he keeps answering about the cards.

At line 11 the flood leaves him 'very draggled'. At line 12 a boy calls him 'a dead mongoose'. By line 37 it is the next morning, and later he meets the cobra. At line 71 Nag, 'at the bottom of his cold heart', is afraid of him. So the creature once taken for dead is now the one the cobra fears.

At line 20 the motto of 'all the mongoose family' is 'Run and find out'. At lines 21 to 23 Rikki-tikki runs round the table and jumps on the boy's shoulder. Lines 68 to 71 say a mongoose cannot 'stay frightened' and must 'fight and eat snakes'. At line 73 his tail fluffs up and he stands up to Nag. So each rule is about all mongooses, but Rikki-tikki is the one who acts it out.

Line 3 calls the blue chair 'a waiting chair'. Lines 4 and 5 say Farhan sat there, got a pencil, and his photograph went up. At line 47 Dilan stands, 'because you stand up when somebody is about to thank you'. So he expects the same sort of thanks that Farhan got. The handle at line 44 shows when he stands, not why.

At line 21 Dilan says 'It goes well, though'. At lines 28 and 29 he calls seven butterflies back out of twelve 'a pass'. Yet lines 29 to 34 list the five still loose, one 'into the kitchen'. At line 36 his mum came 'early for her', and at line 39 he hears 'again'. So he says it went well, but his own details say otherwise.

At line 24 Jo's 'hot temper mastered her'. At line 67 her anger 'took possession of her'. At lines 71 and 72 'the little demon' speaks 'in her ear'. Each time the anger does the acting, and Jo has it done to her. One retold moment alone does not show what the writer keeps doing.

At line 8 the crowd's test is the old saying 'If he's red, he's right'. He takes off his helmet, and at line 9 they cheer him again. Line 61 says the princess could have told him from the King, side by side. Yet at line 63 nobody 'dreamed or imagined' he was anyone but the King. So his hair passes their test, but nobody puts the two men together.

At line 11 he looks 'paler', and at line 13 he is 'a bigger man'. At line 14 someone notices 'a good jaw under that beard'. Each remark notices a difference from the King they know. Yet line 16 calls one 'mere flattery', and line 17 calls them 'signs of approval'. So they keep noticing the difference, but what he hears is approval.

At line 21 Priya 'told nobody' about the nest. Line 22 says a thing not told 'stays exactly the way you left it'. At line 50 she tells Grandad 'Don't get the spray' and 'They're mine'. So the secret she kept is now said out loud, as hers. Her words are about keeping them safe, not about Grandad being stung.

At line 6 they are 'the small traffic' going in and out. At line 14 the wall begins 'to hum', and line 20 shows their 'nest'. At line 43 'Something small' comes out at head height. No line ever says what kind of creature they are. So they are shown over and over, but never named.
